findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the shellcheck AC with det_lint.py:183-190's documented decision to avoid shellcheck: either justify adopting shellcheck as a new prerequisite (and pin/provision it for the in-session test) or reuse/extend the existing bespoke dependency-free lint.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_lint.py:183-190: 'PRIOR ART: shellcheck is the reference lint here ... We keep a BESPOKE, dependency-free, LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC subset rather than shell out to shellcheck (bash-only + a heavy external dep...)'
resolve_symbol('shellcheck') => UNRESOLVED (not a Python dep); shellcheck is a separately-installed external binary, absent from pyproject.toml dependencies
The AC's contract test claim elsewhere in the same section is 'verifiable in-session, not by a future adopter' — a test requiring an unpinned external binary is not in-session guaranteed
findings.finding: The portability AC mandates shellcheck over extracted script bodies, but the repo already made a deliberate, documented prior-art decision NOT to depend on shellcheck (bespoke dependency-free lint instead), and shellcheck is a heavy external binary, not a dependency rebar has — the plan reconciles neither.
findings.location: Portability AC line: 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs, failing loudly on an unparseable config'
scenarios: A contract/CI run on a host without shellcheck installed
Reviewer comparing this AC to the repo's own settled position on shellcheck as prior art
findings.suggested_fix: Cite det_lint.py's prior-art note in the AC and choose explicitly: (a) declare shellcheck a documented tool prerequisite provisioned by the test harness, or (b) route the extracted script bodies through the repo's existing dependency-free verify-command lint, noting why shellcheck's shell-specific checks are/aren't needed here.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how shellcheck is obtained/pinned for the in-session portability gate (mirror the pinned, digest-verified actionlint Makefile target) and require the gate to FAIL — not skip — when shellcheck is unavailable.
evidence: Plan AC: 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs, failing loudly on an unparseable config'
resolve_symbol('shellcheck') = UNRESOLVED (not a Python module; standalone binary)
search Makefile for 'shellcheck' = (no matches); search .pre-commit-config.yaml for 'shell' = (no matches) — no provisioning today
Contrast: Makefile:183-198 installs actionlint as a PINNED, digest-verified binary — the established pattern for external CI tools this AC does not follow
Evidence class: Unverified (tool availability/provisioning not probeable from plan text)
findings.finding: The Portability AC requires shellcheck to run over extracted script bodies as an in-session verification gate, but the plan states no mechanism to obtain/pin the shellcheck binary. shellcheck is a standalone external tool (not a Python dependency), and the repo currently provisions no shellcheck (no Makefile target, no pre-commit hook) — unlike actionlint, which the repo installs via a pinned, SHA-256-verified Makefile target. Without a stated provisioning path this AC may silently no-op on a host lacking shellcheck, exactly the failure mode the plan is trying to eliminate for gh.
findings.location: Portability AC — 'shellcheck runs over script bodies extracted from all three configs, failing loudly on an unparseable config'
scenarios: CI or in-session run on a host without shellcheck on PATH; the gate skips instead of failing
A macOS CI leg (the repo already conditionally skips actionlint on non-Linux) silently drops the shellcheck audit
findings.suggested_fix: Add a repo-local shellcheck provisioning step modeled on the existing `actionlint-bin` Makefile target (pinned version + SHA-256 verification), and specify that the extraction/lint gate exits non-zero if shellcheck cannot be resolved.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the GitLab-schema capability assertion: name the exact schema source (e.g. a pinned, vendored SchemaStore gitlab-ci schema), its version/provenance, and confirm rebar's jsonschema validator handles that draft — rather than asserting a nonexistent 'official offline' artifact.
evidence: pyproject.toml core dependencies = pyyaml, jsonschema, referencing — a validator, but no GitLab schema document is present in the repo

docs.gitlab.com/development/cicd/schema: GitLab's CI/CD schema is Draft-07 and validated internally via monaco-yaml; the widely-consumed editor schema is SchemaStore's gitlab-ci schema (schemastore.org / SchemaStore/schemastore), not a GitLab-published offline artifact
'using dependencies rebar already has' covers the validator (jsonschema) but not the schema document itself, which must be sourced/vendored to validate offline
findings.finding: The AC asserts '.gitlab-ci.yml validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline, using dependencies rebar already has', but rebar ships only a jsonschema validator — no GitLab CI schema document is vendored — and GitLab publishes no standalone offline JSON-schema artifact (the de-facto schema is SchemaStore's gitlab-ci schema; GitLab's own validation uses an internal monaco-yaml/Draft-07 pipeline). The schema's source, version, and provenance are unresolved.
findings.location: Portability AC line: '.gitlab-ci.yml validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline, using dependencies rebar already has'
scenarios: Running the offline validation with no vendored schema and no network
A future GitLab schema update drifting from a vendored copy of unclear provenance
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the AC to vendor a pinned SchemaStore `gitlab-ci` schema (Draft-07) into the repo and validate it offline with the existing jsonschema dep; document the schema version and an update/refresh policy so 'official' is replaced by a concrete, provenance-tracked source.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how GitLab's official CI JSON schema is vendored/committed and pinned (version + provenance) so the offline validation runs against a real schema, not just relying on jsonschema being installed.
evidence: Plan AC quote: 'validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline, using dependencies rebar already has'
resolve_symbol('jsonschema') = EXISTS; pyproject.toml:64 declares jsonschema>=4.18 in core deps — validator verified
search repo for 'gitlab-ci' = (no matches) — the schema artifact is not present today
Evidence class: Partially-verified (validator exists; the specific schema document/surface is unconfirmed and unsourced)
findings.finding: The AC asserts .gitlab-ci.yml 'validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline, using dependencies rebar already has.' The jsonschema validator is indeed a declared dependency (pyproject.toml:64, jsonschema>=4.18) and imports fine, so the validator is verified. But GitLab's official CI JSON schema is a schema DOCUMENT, not a Python dependency; it is not currently in the repo and must be vendored/committed to validate offline. The plan does not name how the schema artifact is sourced, versioned, or pinned, so 'dependencies rebar already has' does not by itself satisfy the offline requirement.
findings.location: Portability AC — '.gitlab-ci.yml validates against GitLab's official JSON schema, offline, using dependencies rebar already has'
scenarios: Offline CI run where the schema was expected to be fetched over the network — validation cannot proceed
Schema drift: an unpinned/undated GitLab schema copy diverges from the GitLab version the docs target
findings.suggested_fix: Commit a pinned copy of GitLab's CI JSON schema into the repo (with a recorded upstream version/URL provenance) and have the offline test load that committed artifact via the already-present jsonschema validator.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign sole ownership of the `_lib_ops.py:115` exit-policy removal to exactly one of 9895 or f789 and make the other depend on / reference it rather than restate it as its own AC

f789 AC: '`_lib_ops.py`'s divergent exit policy is removed'
f789 body: '`_lib_ops.py:115` raises unless the code is in `(0, 75)` ... must be fixed in the same pass'

scenarios: Both tickets are implemented independently; the second to land finds the policy already removed and either no-ops (leaving its AC unverifiable) or conflicts on the edit
A completion verifier checks each ticket's AC against the code and one ticket's AC ('_lib_ops.py policy removed') cannot be attributed to that ticket's change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the sync default-inversion (reconcile dry-run -> bridge sync mutate) reaches the live 20-minute scheduled job safely: a staged/canary rollout or an explicit, tested rollback path, not a single flip.
evidence: "reconcile meant dry-run via a wrapper; bridge sync mutates, so aliasing would be a silent behaviour change"
"The GHA artifact shipped as an example is the workflow rebar actually runs ... so it is exercised every 20 minutes"
"Pause is remote-persisted ... and cannot wedge a mixed-version fleet" — coexistence is addressed for pause but not for the sync default inversion on the live scheduled job
findings.finding: The bridge is a scheduled production job (GHA every 20 minutes) whose default inverts from dry-run to mutate when `reconcile` is retired with no alias, but the plan specifies no staged rollout or rollback path for that behavior flip — only pause's mixed-version safety is addressed.
findings.location: Decisions already taken: "`reconcile` is retired with NO alias ... `bridge sync` mutates"; AC "The GHA artifact ... exercised every 20 minutes"
scenarios: The 20-minute scheduled workflow is updated to call `bridge sync` (mutating) where the old `reconcile` was dry-run; on first tick after deploy it mutates the tracker before anyone has validated the new surface, with no canary/flag gate and no stated rollback beyond ad-hoc pause
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC that the first production cutover runs the new workflow in a preview/dry-run posture (or gated pause) until one clean cycle is observed, and document the one-step rollback (revert workflow ref) as tested.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit back-out/rollback note (e.g. revert-commit strategy or how the prior workflow is restored) for the scheduled bridge run given the no-alias retirement.
evidence: 'reconcile is retired with NO alias. The defaults invert'
'The 106-line YAML push loop is deleted'
No back-out/rollback mechanism stated for the scheduled bridge run
findings.finding: The epic performs multiple destructive, hard-to-reverse changes (retire three verbs with no alias, invert sync defaults, delete a 106-line YAML push loop) but states no rollback/back-out plan if the new surface breaks the every-20-minute CI job after release.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (verb removal, default inversion, YAML deletion)
scenarios: New surface has a defect and the scheduled 20-minute bridge job starts failing with no quick revert path documented

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the pause mechanism so it fails CLOSED on an unrecognised signal for old-version reconcilers (e.g. reuse refs/reconciler/gate with a pause value below every real mode, or a distinct pause ref old binaries treat as blocking), and state how this prevents the named mixed-version wedge given `_mode_blocks` currently treats unknown gate tokens as 'no gate' (fails open).

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'Pause is remote-persisted, carries a reason, and cannot wedge a mixed-version fleet'
scenarios: Operator runs `bridge pause` during a fleet rollout where some runners still ship the previous reconciler; the old binary reads the pause token, fails to recognise it, treats it as no-gate, and reconciles anyway — the fleet is NOT actually paused
A corrupt/partial pause write is read by a mixed fleet with divergent fail-open/fail-closed semantics

scenarios: A client without GitHub Actions runs `bridge fsck --repair`; today the gh guard silently no-ops (portability bug); after gh removal, if nothing replaces it, a live destructive repair on GHA loses the 'suspend the schedule' protection the code relied on
